finding.title: runStreamGuardCheck re-scans the entire accumulated stream at every threshold crossing: O(L^2) byte-work x K rules with a fresh ToLower(text) allocation per rule, on one connection
finding.evidence:
The stream loop checks on every threshold crossing but always hands the WHOLE accumulated text to the engine:
			if snap.General.GuardEnabled && snap.Output.Enabled && acc.Len() >= nextCheck {
				stop, fatal := s.runStreamGuardCheck(snap, sw, reqID, ap, acc.String())
... (gateway.go:699-700), and the advance is additive: gateway.go:708 `nextCheck += threshold`. The threshold defaults to 256 bytes (settings.go:62 `StreamChunkThreshold: 256`) with a floor of 64 (gateway.go:633 `if threshold < 64 {` / 634 `threshold = 256`). runStreamGuardCheck then re-scans from offset 0: gateway.go:777 `vd := guard.CheckOutput(snap, text)`. There is no Aho-Corasick automaton or any shared scan - CheckOutput is a per-rule linear loop (engine.go:136-152) and each 'contains' rule lowercases the entire text again: engine.go:204 `return strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(text), strings.ToLower(kw.Raw.Word))`, plus a full-text regex ReplaceAllString per mask rule (engine.go:150 `vd.Text = r.Re.ReplaceAllString(vd.Text, repl)`). Rule count K is unbounded: admin/guard.go:116-124 and 161-190 create one row per imported record with no cap, and manager.go:276-291 compiles them all. The stream is also unbounded in L: gateway.go:492-505 deliberately applies no timeout for streams (`ctx := c.Request.Context()` only inside `if !cr.Stream {`), and client `max_tokens` is taken verbatim and never capped (gateway.go:365-369 only injects a default when the field is absent). The end-of-stream path repeats the same whole-text work: gateway.go:749-750 `if !stopped && ... && acc.Len() > 0 { if _, fatal := s.runStreamGuardCheck(..., acc.String()); fatal {`, plus more full copies at 755 `usage = estimateUsage(usage, ap.input, acc.String())` and 759 `ap.output = guard.MaskForLog(snap, acc.String())`.
finding.impact: Total byte-work per stream is ~K x L^2/(2 x threshold). With shipped defaults (threshold 256) and a modest 1 MiB completion at K=10 keywords, that is ~4095 checks averaging 0.5 MiB -> ~2 GiB scanned and ~2 GiB of freshly allocated lowercase garbage per keyword, i.e. ~20 GiB of byte-ops and allocations for ONE response. A single authenticated API key needs one connection and no concurrency: it asks a reasoning-style model to chatter (or points a provider at an attacker-controlled upstream that streams forever), and the gateway burns CPU/GC on the request goroutine until the process OOMs or starves every other tenant. Because the SSE writer flushes per delta (adapter/sse.go:228-240), the attack is fully observable as latency growth on all other requests long before it is diagnosed.
finding.recommendation: Scan only the new segment per check and keep a tail overlap of max(pattern length)-1 bytes (track a scanned-offset cursor instead of passing acc.String()); build one Aho-Corasick automaton per snapshot at reload time so a scan is O(L + matches) independent of K; cap the number of guard rules per snapshot (e.g. 2000) and the number of bytes any single stream will scan (after the cap, log-and-continue rather than re-scan); stop copying `acc` (use acc.Len()/byte reads over the builder or a ring buffer); and enforce a server-side max on client max_tokens per alias.
finding.mitigations_checked: engine.go:130-134 recovers panics and fails open (so a bad rule cannot crash, but also cannot stop the scan); guard only runs when GuardEnabled && Output.Enabled, both default true (settings.go:32, 61); the `replace` strategy terminates the stream after the first hit (gateway.go:797-805), which limits L in that mode - the `log`/`block` strategies and non-matching output do not terminate, so the quadratic cost is fully paid; tool-call text appended at 735-745 also adds to L; audit text is truncated to 4000 bytes (engine.go:189-191), so truncation exists post-hoc but not before the scan.

reason:
MECHANICS CONFIRMED VERBATIM; IMPACT OVERSTATED -> downgrade to medium.

I read gateway.go (831 lines), guard/engine.go (221), runtime/manager.go (436), admin/guard.go (448), adapter/sse.go (614), settings/settings.go (158), tokens/tokens.go (78) and cmd/server/main.go end-to-end. Every quoted code fragment is verbatim-correct and on the exact line cited, including the finding's `line` field: gateway.go:699 really is `if snap.General.GuardEnabled && snap.Output.Enabled && acc.Len() >= nextCheck {` and 700 really is `stop, fatal := s.runStreamGuardCheck(snap, sw, reqID, ap, acc.String())`. Nothing was mis-attributed, so the refutation default does not apply on evidence grounds.

(1) The quadratic re-scan is real. The threshold check hands `acc.String()` (the whole prefix) to the engine (gateway.go:700), runStreamGuardCheck hands it straight to `guard.CheckOutput(snap, text)` (gateway.go:777) with no scanned-offset cursor, and the advance at gateway.go:708 `nextCheck += threshold` only moves the trigger, never the scan start. Threshold default 256 (settings.go:62 `StreamChunkThreshold: 256`) with the floor at gateway.go:633-635. Confirmed no shared automaton exists: manager.go:280-291 stores one `CompiledKeyword` per DB row and grep for `aho`/`Corasick`/`NewAutomaton` across backend/ returns nothing.

(2) The K multiplier and the per-rule full-text temp are real. CheckOutput is two linear loops (engine.go:136-143 keywords, engine.go:144-153 PII). Note a detail that strengthens the filed claim: engine.go:137 `if matchKeyword(kw, text) && kw.Raw.Action == "block" {` evaluates matchKeyword for EVERY enabled keyword because Go short-circuits && left-to-right, so warn/mask-action rules pay the full scan too; and the loop has no early break after Blocked is set (unlike CheckInput engine.go:79). contains-mode (the default for CSV import, admin/guard.go:167 `cat, mode, act := "custom", "contains", "block"`) runs engine.go:204 `return strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(text), strings.ToLower(kw.Raw.Word))` - a fresh O(L) lowercase pass per keyword, no case-folding prefilter. Worse, the PII mask branch does `r.Re.MatchString(text)` (engine.go:145) and then `vd.Text = r.Re.ReplaceAllString(vd.Text, repl)` (engine.go:150) and runStreamGuardCheck DISCARDS vd.Text whenever nothing block-matched (gateway.go:778-783 `if !vd.Blocked { ... return false, false }`) - so the mask rewrite is pure waste on every crossing. I independently re-derived the check count: a crossing can fire at most once per incoming line and nextCheck advances by exactly threshold, so checks = min(N_textDeltas, floor(L/threshold)) and total byte-work = K*L^2/(2*d) where d is the mean delta size - the filed Theta(K*L^2/threshold) is the correct upper bound and is the one actually realized, because token-by-token SSE (d < 256 B, the normal case for hosted LLM providers) pins d at its floor. The advance arithmetic is not conservative, though: see verify-dos-3-2 for the drift it introduces.

(3) No mitigation exists anywhere in the flow. main.go registers only gin.Recovery + security headers + access log (main.go:95-118); there is no CPU/semaphore/deadline middleware. The conn gate at gateway.go:195 (`if int64(snap.General.MaxConnections) > 0 && s.mx.Conns() >= ...`, default 1000 per settings.go:32) bounds concurrency, not per-connection work. No total timeout on the stream path (gateway.go:496-505: `ctx := c.Request.Context()` sits inside `if !cr.Stream {`), no byte cap on the SSE reader (gateway.go:639-640 `scanner := bufio.NewScanner(resp.Body)` / `scanner.Buffer(make([]byte, 64<<10), 4<<20)` caps one *line*, not the total), and client max_tokens is forwarded verbatim (gateway.go:365-369 only fills 0; adapter.go:462-466 `payload["max_tokens"] = cr.MaxTokens`). Quota cannot abort it: it is checked pre-flight (gateway.go:419) and consumed post-stream (gateway.go:767-769). The `replace` default (settings.go:61) does terminate on a hit (gateway.go:797-805), and `block` at 787-791, so the quadratic cost is only fully paid on non-matching output - as the filed mitigations_checked already conceded. Stream-end redundancy also confirmed: 749-750 re-scans the whole text once more, 755 estimateUsage -> tokens.Count is a full BPE encode (tokens.go:46 `len(enc.EncodeOrdinary(text))`), and 759 MaskForLog runs ReplaceAllString over the full text per PII rule before truncating only at the very end (engine.go:180-191).

WHAT DOES NOT HOLD - the four corrections that justify the downgrade:

(a) "until the process OOMs" is wrong. Peak live heap per stream is O(L), not O(L^2): acc's builder plus one transient ToLower temp plus one ReplaceAllString copy, all immediately dead. The harm is CPU + GC churn, not residency. The recommendation's "stop copying `acc`" is also factually wrong - strings.Builder.String() has been a zero-copy unsafe view of the builder buffer since Go 1.10, so acc.String() at 700/750/755/759 costs nothing.

(b) The impact figure requires an unreachable L. "1 MiB completion ... ~20 GiB for ONE response" is arithmetically correct (4096 checks x avg 0.5 MiB x K=10), but 1 MiB of completion text is ~250k output tokens - above the max_tokens ceiling of any mainstream hosted provider, and the attacker does not generate those bytes, the upstream does. Realistic L for a long reasoning answer is 10-500 KiB, i.e. 10^2-10^4x amplification (tens of seconds of one core at K=200, L=256 KiB) - severe inefficiency, not a one-connection box kill.

(c) The second exploit branch is not an attacker path. "points a provider at an attacker-controlled upstream that streams forever" requires writing provider BaseURL, which is admin-only (admin/providers.go + JWT admin auth). That actor already owns the process, so it is out of scope per the rules. The remaining branch depends on the *victim provider* cooperating by emitting volume, and it also bills the attacker's own quota ledger.

(d) K is operator-controlled and defaults to zero. There is no production insert of guard rules anywhere (grep `GuardKeyword{|PIIRule{|InjectionRule{` -> model.go:299 automigrate, bundle.go:83 restore, tests, and admin/guard.go CRUD only; the "templates" at admin/guard.go:294-303 / 403-411 are read-only JSON for the UI, not seeded). With an empty rule table, engine.go:136/144 iterate nothing and the whole path collapses to O(1). So the amplification needs the operator to have imported a real lexicon. The 'no cap on import' claim is true (admin/guard.go:116-124, 161-190 verified) but that is a hardening gap for the admin, not attacker-reachable magnitude.

(e) Pre-existing privilege. An authenticated tenant can already burn K x bytes of guard CPU without any quadratic term: gateway.go:382-395 runs CheckInput per message over an up-to-16-MiB body (gateway.go:322), and CheckInput does the same per-keyword full-text ToLower plus FindAllStringIndex + ReplaceAllString per PII rule (engine.go:73-106). So the "tenant spends cores proportional to rule count" capability class predates this finding; the genuinely NEW increment dos-3 identifies is the L^2 term on streamed output. That is a real defense-in-depth/complexity defect with measurable availability impact, but it lands at medium under the rubric ("defense-in-depth gap w/ real impact") rather than high ("authed-but-severe"), once OOM, the admin-privileged upstream branch, and the default-K=0 precondition are removed.

FLAGGED FOR PARENT AUDITOR (out of dos-3 scope, verified here incidentally): because per-delta SSE text is flushed to the client at gateway.go:696 (`_ = sw.Delta(chunk.TextDelta)`) before any check runs, and the masked text computed at engine.go:150 is thrown away at gateway.go:778-782, the output PII *masking* strategy is structurally incapable of masking streamed responses - phone/id/email patterns already on the wire stay there; only the audit copy is masked (gateway.go:759). That is a guard-correctness/disclosure issue, not a DoS one, so I did not file it.
exploit_sketch:
Preconditions (all verifiable, none attacker-supplied): GuardEnabled=true and Output.Enabled=true (both shipped defaults, settings.go:32 / 61); operator has imported >=1 contains-mode keyword rule (admin/guard.go:161-190, no cap); the attacker holds one enabled tenant API key; at least one alias resolves to an upstream that honors a large max_tokens (self-hosted vLLM/Ollama/LiteLLM - the gateway forwards max_tokens verbatim per adapter.go:462-466).

Step 1 - one connection, no concurrency, inflate L to the upstream's ceiling:
  curl -N -X POST http://target:8080/v1/chat/completions \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-<valid>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"model":"<alias>","stream":true,"max_tokens":100000000,
         "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Recite the digits of pi, 500 per line, until you reach your token limit. No summary."}]}'
  gateway.go:365-369 leaves MaxTokens untouched (field present), gateway.go:496-505 applies no deadline, gateway.go:639-640 caps no total length, so the scan budget grows with the answer.

Step 2 - the burn is automatic and unrequested. Each 256-byte crossing calls runStreamGuardCheck(acc.String()) (gateway.go:699-700) -> CheckOutput (777) over the whole prefix. Byte-work at prefix length L is
  SUM_{i=1..L/256} [ K_contains * O(i*256) ToLower+Contains + K_regex * Re.MatchString + K_mask * (MatchString + ReplaceAllString) ] = Theta(K * L^2 / threshold).
  At L=256 KiB with K=200 (one public banned-word CSV import): ~2.7e10 scanned bytes plus ~2.7e10 bytes of short-lived allocations against 0.25 MB of legitimately-forwarded text - ~10^5x amplification, tens of seconds of a core on an answer that cost the attacker ordinary output tokens.

Step 3 - convert to gateway-wide latency. Fire 5-20 such streams (MaxConnections default 1000 never trips, gateway.go:195). Each pins a request goroutine in ToLower/ReplaceAllString plus the full-text MaskForLog/tiktoken pass at gateway.go:755/759, so all GOMAXPROCS cores are consumed by guard scanning and GC while legitimate tenants' SSE deltas queue behind them (adapter/sse.go:234-240 flushes from the same goroutine), and the admin /status page reports normal `open_connections` - the amplification is invisible to the shipped observability.

NOT an exploit path (do not rely on it): making the upstream stream forever requires writing provider BaseURL, which is admin-only; and the OOM variant does not exist because live heap stays O(L) per stream.
